channel.title: Adler & Rochefort — Insights
channel.description: Insurance in Portugal and Spain, explained.

item.title: Allianz Care vs Cigna Global: international health insurance for families in Portugal and Spain
item.description: Two of the international health plans families in Portugal and Spain ask us about most, set side by side: how each is built, what it covers and who each one suits.

item.title: Classic and high-value car insurance in Spain: historic status, agreed value and collections
item.description: Spain rewrote its historic vehicle rules in 2024. What that means for a classic, how agreed value works, and what a collection or a supercar in Marbella actually needs.

item.title: High-value home insurance in Portugal and Spain: the conditions, clause by clause
item.description: The clauses that separate a private-client household policy from the standard multirriscos — what each one does, and why it matters on the day of a claim.

item.title: Art and jewellery cover beyond the agreed value: underinsurance, defective title, commissions and loans
item.description: Agreed value settles the obvious question. These are the less obvious ones a collector meets: a market that moved, a disputed title, a commission in progress, a loan to a museum.

item.title: Family protection in a high-value home policy: carjacking, home invasion, stalking and kidnap expenses
item.description: Some of the risks a wealthy family faces have nothing to do with the building. The best household policies cover them anyway — here is what that cover does, and where its limits are.

item.title: What you must tell the insurer: the obligations behind a high-value home policy
item.description: The best wording in the market can still fail on a claim if something was not declared. A practical list of what to tell the insurer, when, and what to do after a loss.

item.title: D&O insurance for holding companies and family offices
item.description: Owners who also manage, relatives as shareholders, money moving between entities: why D&O for a family holding is different, and how to structure it.

item.title: One programme for several homes, a yacht and a collection
item.description: A house in Lisbon, a villa in Mallorca, a yacht and a collection that travels between them: how a coordinated programme replaces five unrelated policies.

item.title: Crime, payment fraud and cyber cover for a family office
item.description: A family office moves large sums on the instruction of a few trusted people. Why that makes it a target, and how crime and cyber cover respond.

item.title: Kidnap and ransom cover in a family office programme
item.description: K&R is the policy a family hopes never to use. How a family office decides who it covers, who knows about it, and how it fits the rest of the programme.

item.title: Portugal, a surf nation — and the second homes it attracts
item.description: From the giant waves of Nazaré to the reefs of Ericeira and the two coasts of Sagres: why Portugal became a surf nation, the second homes it attracts, and what protecting one involves.

item.title: Surfing Ericeira — and owning a home at Europe’s first World Surfing Reserve
item.description: Seven world-class waves in four kilometres, forty-five minutes from Lisbon. The surf, the town, the homes Lisbon families and international buyers choose, and how to protect them.

item.title: Surfing Nazaré — big waves, the canyon and a home on the Silver Coast
item.description: How a submarine canyon made a fishing town the capital of big-wave surfing, where residents surf on ordinary days, the homes on the Silver Coast, and the insurance points specific to Nazaré.

item.title: Surfing Sagres — two coasts at the end of Europe, and a home on the cliffs
item.description: West coast or south coast: why Sagres is surfable almost every day, the waves and the way of life at the end of Europe, the homes the natural park allows, and how to protect them.

item.title: Surfing Aljezur — Arrifana, Amado and a home on the Costa Vicentina
item.description: The greenest, wildest stretch of the Algarve: its beaches and waves, a slow outdoor culture, restored farmhouses on large plots — and wildfire, the risk that defines the hinterland.

item.title: Surfing from Lagos — two coasts within reach, and a home in a year-round town
item.description: Lagos surfs on its own beaches in winter and has the whole west coast half an hour away. The town, the homes surfing families choose, and what protecting them involves.

item.title: Golf in Portugal and Spain: the great courses, the communities and the homes on the fairway
item.description: The courses and communities that made Iberia Europe’s golf address, the homes built around them, and what protecting a house on the fairway actually involves.

item.title: Marinas and yachts in Portugal and Spain: from the Atlantic to the Balearics
item.description: From Atlantic passages via Madeira and the Azores to the Balearic summer: the marinas, the waterfront homes, and what a yacht and a house by the water need.

item.title: Insuring a high-value home in Madeira: quintas, slopes and the island perils
item.description: The south coast sits on steep volcanic catchments. Storm, flood and landslip are different lines in a Portuguese wording, and the 2010 aluvião is why the distinction matters.

item.title: Luxury condos and resort homes: where the building policy ends
item.description: The association covers the shared fabric. You cover the interior, the contents, and the way the home is actually used — lived in, let, empty or mixed.

item.title: Art in the house is not automatically insured
item.description: A household limit is written for furniture. A collection needs to be scheduled, and told where the piece actually is, including a second home in the other country.

item.title: Insuring an Irish-owned holiday home in the Algarve
item.description: What changes when an Algarve property is a holiday home rather than a permanent residence: vacancy conditions, Alojamento Local, and the sum insured.

item.title: US umbrella insurance vs. Portuguese liability cover
item.description: Why a US umbrella policy stays behind, what Portugal has instead, and what to actually check on your Portuguese home and car policies.

item.title: Claiming in Portugal when you are used to a US adjuster
item.description: No single adjuster relationship, a written process by default, and what the actual claims sequence looks like in Portugal.

item.title: Liability insurance for yoga instructors in Portugal
item.description: Not on the regulated list, but the exposure — and the venues asking for proof of cover — are real.

item.title: Liability insurance for Pilates and Tai Chi instructors in Portugal
item.description: Equipment risk, hands-on correction and older student bases — the real exposure behind two unregulated disciplines.

item.title: Liability insurance for massage and spa therapists in Portugal
item.description: Not a physiotherapist, not an osteopath, not one of the regulated six — what massage-therapist liability cover actually needs to reflect.

item.title: What a Total-Loss Settlement Actually Covers, and the Order It's Worked Out In
item.description: Demolition, professional fees, VAT and alternative accommodation — the nine-step order a loss adjuster actually works through after a total loss.

item.title: Setting the Rebuild Value: Getting to a Number That Holds Up
item.description: How to reach a defensible rebuild value for a property in Portugal or Spain: cost per m² by construction type, pools and annexes, finishes, demolition and fees.

item.title: Waiver of Average: What It Is, and What It Costs to Have
item.description: What a waiver of average does, which property wordings in Portugal and Spain offer a form of it, and the conditions for setting the proportional rule aside.
